destination.name: Rakiraki
destination.tagline: Viti Levu's Suncoast, with island diving, sunset beaches and early settlement sites
destination.description: Rakiraki sits on the north coast of Viti Levu, on a strip of land known as the Suncoast. Nananu-i-Ra, a small island reached by boat from Ellington Wharf, has resorts, the One Bay beach and well-known dive sites. On the mainland, the tomb of the 19th-century chief Ratu Udre Udre lies near Vaileka. Navatu Rock stands beside Kings Road in Vitawa village, one of Fiji's oldest settlement sites.
whyVisit: Dive reefs off a small island

goodToKnow.title: Boat to Nananu-i-Ra
goodToKnow.detail: The island is reached by boat from Ellington Wharf, so plan your transfers around the crossing.

goodToKnow.title: Quick stop on Kings Road
goodToKnow.detail: Navatu Rock is a roadside look in Vitawa village and Ratu Udre Udre's tomb is a short stop, so combine them.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}, the cooler months, for boat trips and dives. Cyclones can occur Nov to Apr.

rakiraki-1.bio: A small island off the Rakiraki coast, reached by chartered boat from the mainland and known for diving and kayaking.

rakiraki-3.bio: Tomb of the 19th-century chief Ratu Udre Udre, listed by Guinness as the most prolific cannibal, near Rakiraki.

rakiraki-4.bio: Sacred rock by Kings Road at Vitawa village that looks like a man or woman from different angles.
